dedupe_keys.name: mugs model of urban green spaces

description: MUGS is an abstract model of what drives inequality in contact with nature within and between cities. It tests a social integration hypothesis: people decide whether to visit an urban green space mainly by judging who else is likely to be there at the same time, and that judgement runs mostly along class lines. The model simulates four cities in Scotland and shows under which conditions these mechanisms are enough to reproduce the observed inequalities in green space use. Version 0.5.9 was published by Stefano Picascia on CoMSES in September 2021. Coverage: four Scottish cities. Access: free NetLogo code on CoMSES. Licence: CC-BY-SA-4.0. Caveats: an abstract explanatory model, not a forecast of visits. Simulation uses are testing how green space provision and social mix change who benefits from parks, for example for heat refuge and wellbeing planning. Related records: the Krakow sport facility location model and the local sports communities model.
inputs: Four Scottish cities with green spaces and neighbourhoods
Residents' social class and visit decisions
name: MUGS: Model of Urban Green Spaces
outputs: Use of urban green spaces by class and inequality in contact with nature
